newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas up sharply, follows gains on OTC market.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas up sharply, follows gains on OTC market.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures market rose sharply on Friday morning, catching up with the gains made on the physical market on Thursday evening, and with a healthy volume of trade done for the first time this week.
"It's most definitely following physical," said a futures broker, adding that "offers are getting hit" and there was no other significant news influencing prices.

The first trades of the session were for the three months in the first quarter next year, all done at the same time, possibly as a strip. In each of the three months the price reached a contract high, and the average of the three was 16.866 pence a therm. This compares with trade done on the physical market at up to 17.00 pence on Thursday evening before prices started to soften slightly.

Deals were later done in every month from July to November, with prices up by 0.25 pence a therm in each month except August, which rose by 0.275 pence. Only one trade was done in each month, but the total volume in the morning, 200 lots, was the highest of the week and more than is often done over a whole day.
